documents.title: Infectious Diseases Clinic Letter
documents.author: infectious diseases
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Your patient completed six weeks of ampicillin and ceftriaxone for ampicillin-susceptible E. faecalis endocarditis of the native tricuspid valve on 1/25. His PICC was removed on 1/26 and two surveillance blood cultures drawn the same day have no growth at five days. Weekly monitoring labs were unremarkable throughout. He has had no fever since the second hospital day and reports normal appetite and energy.

Exam today: afebrile, heart regular without murmur, PICC site healed, no peripheral stigmata.

Assessment: enterococcal tricuspid endocarditis, treated. Genitourinary source after cystolitholapaxy.

Recommendations:
- End-of-therapy transthoracic echo, ordered for 2/10.
- Because of prior endocarditis he should receive antibiotic prophylaxis before dental procedures that involve the gums or tooth roots: amoxicillin 2 g by mouth 30 to 60 minutes before. Please prescribe as needed.
- Report any fever promptly and have blood cultures drawn before any antibiotic.

No routine ID follow-up after the echo if it is reassuring.

Infectious Diseases

reports.text:
INDICATION: Completed therapy for tricuspid valve endocarditis.
COMPARISON: TTE 12/12/2025.
FINDINGS: Normal left ventricular size, wall thickness and systolic function, LVEF 60%. Normal right ventricular size and function. Tricuspid valve leaflets thin and mobile; no vegetation seen. Aortic, mitral and pulmonic valves normal. Normal valve function. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: No residual vegetation. Normal valve function. LVEF 60%.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after E. faecalis tricuspid IE. Finished 6 wk ampicillin/ceftriaxone 1/25, PICC out 1/26, surveillance cultures no growth (ID letter reviewed). End-of-therapy TTE 2/10: no vegetation, normal valve function, EF 60%.

Feels fully recovered. Back to walking. No fever, night sweats, SOB or swelling. Voiding about as before; some hesitancy.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Heart regular, no murmur now. Lungs clear. Old PICC site healed. No edema.

A/P
1. Hx enterococcal IE, treated - per ID, dental prophylaxis from now on. He has a cleaning in March - will send amoxicillin. Fever = call before any antibiotic, cultures first.
2. BPH with chronic retention - urology in April. Copy of ID letter and echo to urology so they have the history.
3. HTN - continue. BMP, CBC today.
RTC May.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Cleaning is next Thursday the 19th. The dental office asked if I need the antibiotic.

documents.title: RE: Dentist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes - sent amoxicillin to your pharmacy. Take all 4 capsules together 30-60 minutes before the appointment. Gave you a few extra doses' worth with refills so you have it for future visits. Bring the bottle so the dentist can note it.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Thanks for forwarding the infectious diseases records; noted for any future procedure.

He is five months out from cystolitholapaxy. Stream is better than last fall, no infections, no hematuria. Bladder scan post-void residual today 95 mL.

Impression: BPH with chronic retention, much improved emptying after the stone was cleared.

Plan: continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. Outlet surgery not needed at this point. Recheck residual in 6-12 months.

Urology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine BP check. Spring has been quiet. Dental cleaning in March went fine with the amoxicillin. Urology in April: residual down to 95, no surgery for now.
Home BP 124-134 / 76-82. No side effects.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, amoxicillin 2 g before dental work. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
HTN - controlled, no change. BMP today.
Hx IE - prophylaxis in place, no fevers.
BPH - per urology.
Wellness visit in September.
